Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed next steps for the POC so we can align before we draft the statement of work: 

1) Business goal: Reduce support-handling time by surfacing accurate suggested replies and triage labels for Tier 1 tickets.
2) Key success criteria (proposed):
   - Suggested reply acceptance rate >= 40% during live shadow (measured by agent accept/copy rate)
   - Mean time-to-first-suggestion under 2.5s (p99 under 4s)
   - Labeling F1 >= 0.75 on Acme QA testset

3) Evaluation plan options we discussed:
   - Offline evals: run batch inference on historical tickets (holdout set) using our eval rubric; results will be deterministic and help tune thresholds.
   - Online shadow: route 10–20% of live traffic in shadow mode to measure accept rate and latency end-to-end.

4) Proposed timeline: 6 weeks from kick-off
   - Week 0: Kick-off & secure data access
   - Week 1–2: Offline evals and tuning
   - Week 3–4: Private sandbox integration + online shadowing
   - Week 5–6: Final validation and handoff

I've attached a draft POC plan and an initial eval rubric (Acme-POC-plan-v1.pdf, Acme-eval-rubric.xlsx). Can you confirm: 1) these success criteria look aligned to your team, 2) any constraints (data residency, security) we should bake in, and 3) whether Tom (copied) should be the technical owner on your side?

If that looks good, I'll loop in Dev (SE) and Lauren (CS) to own the implementation and monitoring.

Thanks,

Hey Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Overall this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the acceptance rate target is reasonable; could we make a pass/fail threshold of 40% but aim for a stretch goal of 55%? Also want to track degradation rate (% of suggestions that are worse than baseline).
- Latency: 2.5s mean is fine but p99 under 3.5s would be ideal for our SLA.
- Data residency: Acme requires that all ticket content used for offline evals remains in our EU region. For the shadow traffic we'll need to ensure no PII is logged by Redwood outside agreed buckets and that audit logs are enabled.
- Timeline: 6 weeks is acceptable, but we need the kick-off in the next two weeks. Tom will be technical owner and will coordinate infra access.

Can you confirm SE will do the offline evaluation and provide the raw metrics + evaluation spreadsheet? Also please include a short grading rubric for online shadow (how accept rate maps to pass/fail and how human review will be handled).

Thanks Marissa —

I can take the offline evals and draft the online shadow rubric. Quick notes / plan: 

1) EU data residency: we can run offline evals in our EU region (Frankfurt) if Acme provides a S3 bucket/transfer link in the EU. We will not pull data out of that region; results spreadsheet will contain only aggregated metrics unless Acme explicitly authorizes otherwise.

2) Offline eval methodology: 
   - Use a holdout of 5k anonymized historical tickets (stratified by category).
   - Run model variants (baseline vs candidate) and compute: suggestion acceptance proxy (simulated), label F1, token-level perplexity, and latency distribution.
   - Output: metrics spreadsheet (per-ticket scores anonymized), summary dashboard, and recommended thresholds. Target delivery: Mon, 16 Feb.

3) Online shadow rubric (draft):
   - Traffic split: 15% shadow for first 2 weeks, ramp to 25% if stable.
   - Scoring per suggestion: human reviewer rate on a 0–3 scale:
       3 = Perfect (no edit needed; acceptable to send as-is)
       2 = Useful (small edits required; saves >30s for agent)
       1 = Partial (suggestion may help but requires substantial edits)
       0 = Bad (incorrect or harmful)
   - Pass/fail mapping:
       - Pass if average score >= 2.0 and acceptance rate >= 40% over a sliding 7-day window.
       - Warning if average score in [1.5,2.0) or acceptance rate in [30%,40%).
       - Fail if average score < 1.5 or acceptance rate < 30% (require rollback).
   - Human review workflow: Lauren to coordinate a lightweight panel (5 agents) to rate a random stratified sample of 200 suggestions per week. Reviews stored in Acme-only EU bucket.

4) Monitoring & telemetry: we will surface the following in the console: per-route acceptance rate, avg suggestion score, latency p50/p95/p99, and anonymized examples flagged as Bad. Audit logs will be enabled and shared as agreed.

If that aligns, I'll run the offline jobs this week (in EU) and upload the spreadsheet to the Drive link.
